import html # Example template; in real usage this would be provided externally. html_template = """ Response
{user_content}
""" def construct_html_response(content: str) -> str: """ Injects the user-provided content into an HTML template after escaping it. Args: content: The raw string supplied by the user that will be inserted into the template. Returns: A complete HTML string with the escaped user content embedded. """ # Escape special HTML characters to prevent XSS or markup injection escaped_content = html.escape(content, quote=True) # Insert the escaped content into the template return html_template.format(user_content=escaped_content)
